entries.what_happened: One manuscript, 'A smooth three-torus diffeomorphism with simple Lebesgue spectrum' (OpenAI, dated September 23, 2026). Its Theorem 1.1 (thm:main) claims that there exist a C^∞ volume-preserving diffeomorphism T of the three-torus T³ (with normalized standard volume) and a real function f in the mean-zero space L²_0(T³) such that the bilateral orbit {f∘Tⁿ : n∈Z} is an orthonormal basis of all of L²_0. The same theorem derives that T is ergodic and that the Koopman operator U_T on L²_0 is unitarily equivalent to multiplication by w on L²(S¹, m), which is simple Lebesgue spectrum. The proof is an inductive limit. It builds smooth volume-preserving maps S_n, which are twists (θ,u,a) ↦ (θ+φ(u),u,a) reached through volume-preserving coordinate passages, with observables f_n whose spectral density is made exactly one by a whitening step (§5). The sequence converges in C^∞ to T, and completeness of the orbit comes from approximating a dense family of test functions by Laurent polynomials in U applied to f_n. Section 6 (Corollary 'dynamical-profile') adds mixing, zero entropy and vanishing Lyapunov exponents. Its mixing of order k≥3 depends on a separate OpenAI preprint, 'Rokhlin's multiple-mixing problem for one transformation' (cited as MultipleMixing2026, Theorem 1.1), which I did not read. The abstract says: 'We solve the probability-preserving form of Banach's simple Lebesgue-spectrum problem in smooth dynamics.'
entries.delivers: Existence of an ergodic, probability-preserving, discrete-time (Z-action) system with simple Lebesgue spectrum on its mean-zero L² space. The example is a smooth (C^∞) volume-preserving diffeomorphism of T³ with standard volume. Simple means multiplicity one, and Lebesgue means the spectral type is Haar measure on the circle; both are obtained from one cyclic orbit. The manuscript states its own scope. The abstract restricts the claim to 'the probability-preserving form', and §1 says that formulation is 'distinct from the historical real-line question recorded by Ulam and attributed to Banach'. So the claim is not offered for the infinite-measure line version. The manuscript defines the probability-preserving form in §1 as the Koopman operator on the orthogonal complement of the constants. It does not restate the list's bullet word for word, so this is a reading of that bullet, and the family matches the reading that the problem_asks note names for finite measure and Z-actions. The generator f is only required to lie in L² (real, centered, norm one), so the observable is not smooth. The smoothness claim is for T alone.
entries.remains: If the claim is correct, the probability-preserving, discrete-time reading is answered by existence, and parts (1)–(3) of problem_asks are met under that reading. Left open by this family: the infinite-measure (Ulam, real-line) reading, which the manuscript explicitly sets aside; continuous time (flows and R^d actions), which §1 discusses only through other results (Prikhod'ko, Fayad–Forni–Kanigowski, Abdedou–Fayad–Kessi) without settling the simple-Lebesgue question for flows; and any class of examples other than C^∞ volume-preserving diffeomorphisms of T³ (other manifolds, other regularity classes, analytic maps).
entries.direction: proves existence: a positive answer, constructing an example in the probability-preserving discrete-time form
entries.object: The diffeomorphism T and the generator f are not explicit. They are the limit of an inductive construction (Proposition 'one stage' in §5, then the smooth limit in the proof of Theorem 1.1), and no formula is given. The intermediate maps are explicit twists, but the limit map is specified only as a limit.
entries.doubts: The text flags no step as sketched, hedged or deferred. A search for 'sketch', 'omit', 'routine' and 'left to' found nothing of the kind. The argument is long and compressed, and each stage is a sequence of choices of the form 'arbitrarily small after the earlier finite data are fixed'. The key inputs are the passage lemma (§2), the signal lemma (§3), and the prediction proposition and finite phase-test lemma (§4). I read their statements and only selected passages, so my account of them rests mainly on their statements. The abstract's 'solve' is qualified to the probability-preserving form in the abstract itself, but the title has no such qualification. The mixing corollary's order-≥3 mixing depends on the separate MultipleMixing2026 preprint. Its zero-entropy step uses Rokhlin's finite-multiplicity theorem, and its vanishing-exponent step uses Pesin's formula as stated by Mañé. These are cited rather than proved here, and they are not needed for the spectral claim itself. I found no inconsistency between the abstract and Theorem 1.1.
